utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Anything to raise? Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just one brief matter. Mr. Mehanovic is already commenced and we doubtless we'll finish today. We're going to reach, therefore, Mr. Sakrak today. When I mentioned that I wanted this matter raised, we haven't received it but we've been told that briefing notes -- proofing notes, I should say, are now available online and will be made available at some stage soon. We don't have them for Mr. Husic, and he may -- well, in any event, that's the only notes that we have at this point. Now, we really need to get these proofing notes quicker than we are, Your Honour, because it places us in a difficult position. We don't want to delay the hearing and we want to go on as quickly as we can. There may be good reasons why we're getting them late, but whatever those reasons are, good or not, they place the Defence in an invidious position, because the fact is there's a likelihood of Mr. Sakrak being ready now. So I don't know how to resolve that problem, but I raise it with you now because I'm aware of it now and he's going to come on today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any response? [Prosecution counsel confer].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. With regard to Mr. Sakrak, the notes have been provided by e-mail to Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: (redacted) However, due to that snowstorm or blizzard that they had in the former Yugoslavia, he didn't arrive until late last night. We've only met him for the first time today, and the notes are actually being -- could we redact the second name, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. And they just -- they just met him this morning and the notes are being prepared as we speak. The notes will be provided either by the end of today, or if we meet with him in the morning to confirm what -- what is in the notes, it will be provided tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Which is a day in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. But I hope you could do it as early as possible so that -- to facilitate the proceedings. By the way, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think the Bench has already instructed you to meet with the Defence team to prepare a kind of report on the agreed facts. I also want to know what's the progress of that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I know Mr. Morrissey had met with attorney David Re on the matter. I'm not aware of the results, but I know they had been working together. It might be easier for him to respond to that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we haven't -- that's true. I did meet with Mr. Re, as instructed. We agreed on a number of facts. There are a number more to be discussed, but we have some, it's fair to say, uncontroversial background facts agreed. We just haven't had time; I particularly have not unfortunately had the ability to reduce that into a report sort of a form. They chiefly relate to the sort of uncontroversial matters that Your Honour referred to at the time the discussion took place. I apologise for the delay in providing that report. As Your Honour has probably seen, things are moving fairly quickly on the witness front, although on a minute-to-minute basis they might seem to be moving a bit slowly. In reality things are moving, and that's being the reason we haven't got around to this. So I can indicate that as soon as we have a moment, we will do that, but I would ask the Court's indulgence in relation to it. Mr. Jasarevic is coming. He's a witness -- he's a document witness, and he's -- it's fair to say a high-volume preparation witness. In order to make things move as quickly as we can, we want to have those documents ready to proceed through the e-court system, and it may be that in the following week we would be in a position to assist. I do apologise for it. Your Honour, I understand that Your Honour made that request and gave us an indulgence on a couple of times before. There's nothing that's agreed that will change the nature of the case, if I can put it in those terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And the purpose for this agreed-facts report is to facilitate the proceedings. If the parties submit it too late, it will be useless. But I take the promise from the parties that there might be a report next week. Thank you. And could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a good rest yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Weiner: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Mehanovic.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you testified about leaving Sarajevo, about September 7th, arriving the following day, on the 8th, in Grabovica, and that evening, on the 8th, going to Jablanica for the night, and returning the next day, which would be the 9th at lunchtime. Let's go to that date, September 9th. What did you do when you returned?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was lunchtime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you have your lunch or where did you get your food?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside a house. In the yard of that house was our assembly point. They brought the food. The troops gathered. And the soldiers would pick up their ration and take it wherever they were staying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you receive any instructions when you obtained your food or your lunch?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They told us that somebody from the Supreme Command would come, that some officers would come from the Supreme Command, and that we should get together after lunch, that we should assemble after lunch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then have your lunch?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to step back for a second and ask you a question outside of September 9th. Did -- were there any -- were there any Muslim refugees staying in Grabovica during that time that you were there?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they staying?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the other side of the Neretva in some sort of wooden cabins.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you have any contact -- did you or the other soldiers have any contact with the Muslim refugees?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did not, but others did. I heard from them that they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Let us -- excuse me. Let us return to September 9th. During lunch, was there any discussion in relation to the Muslim refugees?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, stories were going around that some men had come looking for food because they had been starving and they had been in Stolac detained, somewhere near Capljina, where they were captured. That man was saying that they were all mistreated, that all Muslim girls from age 13 to 18 had been raped, that they urinated in their cups of tea and then forced them to drink the tea, and all kinds of stories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's take it step by step. You said "some man." Are you referring to a refugee or a Muslim refugee? This man who was telling these stories.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that he had been detained. Did you learn when he had been released?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure how I came to hear about it, but I seem to remember that they were released seven days after they found accommodation with us or near us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Seven days after or seven days before?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Before. Before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Seven days before we arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you talked about the mistreatment and you said women between the ages of 13 and 18 had been raped and these were Muslim women. What about the women older than 18? Was there any discussion of how they were treated?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 13 to 70. All Muslim women from 13 to 70 years of age.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had been raped?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what the man was saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you said that the man also said that "they would urinate in the cups and then forced them to drink the tea." Who would urinate in the cups?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Croats, I suppose. Who else?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who would be forced to drink the tea and urine?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're not receiving any translation.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The men.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness said: "The men."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you referring to the refugees?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these Muslim refugees, who was detaining them in Stolac or Capljina?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not refugees. They were captives, people who had been captured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was detaining these people?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Herceg-Bosna. What do I know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, people from what ethnic group were detaining these people?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Croats. Croats kept them locked up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you and the other soldiers heard these stories about this mistreatment to the Muslim men and women, how did you feel?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it was hard to hear. How are you supposed to feel? Only who would do such a thing? How do you think it affected us?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you and the other soldiers upset?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we discussed it. Of course it wasn't a simple thing to deal with. What do I know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after hearing these stories, did you and the other soldiers gather in the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at lunch the people who had brought food -- who usually brought food told us that we should assemble later in the courtyard around 2.30 or 3.00 - I'm not sure anymore - because some people from the Supreme Command would come for a visit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you assemble in that courtyard?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did any senior members of the command arrive?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who arrived after you assembled in the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Halilovic, Mr. Karic, and Mr. Zuka, Alispago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were Halilovic, Alispago, and Karic doing after you assembled?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they didn't do anything. They came to inform us about the operation, to ask how we had travelled, if we were happy with the accommodation, if we had any complaints.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did the soldiers respond

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They complained that the Croats who were around would not let us stay in their houses. Things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they say anything else about the Croats, the local Croats from Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, upon further inquiries or in response to their questions regarding accommodation and food, the soldiers complained more about the fact that the Croats would let -- would not let them inside their houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, while this conversation or the complaining was occurring, were there any local residents from Grabovica present?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a man standing on the balcony of that house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the house located in relation to the soldiers and the -- and the meadow there or the -- actually, the courtyard, sir? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can show me a photograph, I will explain it to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, why don't you just try and explain now and then we'll get to a photograph a little later, if you can.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was almost at the end of the village -- well, not at the end of the village. To the right. There was one house behind that house, and then behind that house there was a courtyard in front of that house. I can't really explain it to you. It's not possible for me to explain unless I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the witness please be shown photograph 01494612, which is Exhibit P7, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the photograph in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that help you explain what was happening?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you use one of the marking pencils. The usher will assist you. And please point to the areas. Please show us first where you recall that you were standing.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right here. That was the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, where -- all right. If you could put a "1" next to the circle where the -- which is the area where you were standing, please. If you could put the number "1".

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I -- I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. Sorry, sir. Mr. Mehanovic, could you put a number "1" to the right of that circle which indicates where you and the troops were standing.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I don't quite understand the question. What should I write?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You drew a circle on that photograph of the area where you and the other troops were standing.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just put the number "1" next to that so that later when we look at the picture we know what that refers to. A "1" is where you were standing with the troops. Could you put a number "1" there, the figure 1.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1 that we were lined up there? Is that what you want?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, just write a number "1" next to the circle.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Few very much. Thank you very much. Now, could you show us with a line where the officers were, Halilovic, Alispago, and Karic.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were lined up in this courtyard. It's about 20 metres or maybe more from the house to this road here. We were lined up in one, two, or three rows. I'm not sure. I was, I think, somewhere at the head of the column. Karic was standing next to the corner of the house. And Mr. Halilovic and Mr. Alispago were walking in front of the assembled soldiers and talking to them. This balcony here is where this Croat was standing, from this house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please circle the balcony where the Croat was standing, the Croat man. And could you put a number "2" next to that circle. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may it reflect that there was a number "1" in the circle where the troop were standing and a number "2" within the circle where the Croat man was standing on the balcony. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's have it admitted into the evidence. I guess there's no objections from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, there's no objections, Your Honour, except that I -- I think my friend might be about to mark some more things on it. So if there's going to be some more marked on, perhaps delay it until then; otherwise, we'll have more than one exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I don't oppose it, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think, you know, this is the Prosecution's strategy. You know, whatever they do, we just accept. We cannot, you know, give --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Give them some directions in that aspect. But in the future, if you need the photograph, you can ask the witness to do it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would offer that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P174, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did Mr. Karic say anything in relation to the man on the balcony?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Halilovic and Mr. Alispago were walking around and talking to the soldiers about these problems and acquainting them with the operation that would follow. Karic was standing somewhere around here, at the head of the column, near the corner of the house. And when the soldiers were saying that they were -- that the Croats were complaining and not providing accommodation and so on, Karic then noticed that man and said, "Who is that?" And these other guys said it was an Ustasha, and then he said, "Well, you know what you will do and how you will deal with him," something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Karic said, "Who's the man on the balcony," who responded, "He's an Ustasha"?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those people from the first column, at the head of the column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're talking about soldiers that were in the columns of the lines?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how -- what you recall he responded -- Mr. Karic responded.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he said -- when they said, "He was an Ustasha," and they said that "He was the one who complained the most," then he said, "Well, then you know what to do with him and how you will deal with him," something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the soldiers remain in line?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 15 or 20 minutes, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you saw Mr. Halilovic there. Do you know a man -- or prior to September of 1993, did you know a man named Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you first come to know of him?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I saw him was in the Presidency building, when we were securing that building in the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "we were securing," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many times while you were securing or guarding the Presidency building did you see Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure how many times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it just a few or are you talking about something occurring often?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes it would happen that we would have breakfast in the same place. Mr. Halilovic, Mr. Siber, and Mr. Jovan Divjak were in the General Staff at the time, and sometimes we would have breakfast or lunch or dinner at the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you ever see Sefer Halilovic meeting or visiting with Ramiz Delalic, known as Celo, at Celo's base?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, once in Saburina, when we were the 3rd Mountain Brigade, in September or October. I'm not sure. In 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you ever present when this same Celo, also known as Ramiz Delalic, met with Sefer Halilovic at Halilovic's office or at one of the government buildings?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never present at such a meeting, but I did go once or twice to the General Staff, but I don't know, I never actually attended the talks or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to the General Staff meeting, although you didn't go inside and attend the meeting itself, when you went to the building where it was held, was Ramiz Delalic, Celo, with you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was Sefer Halilovic on the General Staff at that time?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd ask you to look around this courtroom, and could you tell me if Sefer Halilovic is in the courtroom at this time.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please identify him. Point him out, please.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us where he is in the courtroom or what he's wearing, for the record.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's sitting up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, there's -- there's five gentlemen sitting over there. Could you just tell me which one or what -- tell me what type of clothing he's wearing.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only see one there; Mr. Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is he in relation to the wall?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this seems like a quiz to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Since there are several -- there are five men sitting there, could you please stand, with the Court's permission, and point him out, because -- could he -- could the witness come in the middle and point him out, please. Or is the Court going to accept --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, could I indicate that -- Mr. Halilovic, I'm sure, would have no difficulty in standing briefly for the purposes of being identified by this witness, if it needs to be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't think he is essentially important in this proceedings to ask a witness to identify somebody, you know, because, you know, it's -- it's not like a line-up in a police station, you know, there. So I think the witness has already done his best. You know, there's no doubts about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, may the record reflect that the witness was -- the witness has identified the defendant Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Shall we move on?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after this visit by Mr. Karic, Mr. Alispago, and Mr. Halilovic and -- or Sefer Halilovic, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they finished and when they left, I went to Jablanica, a half an hour or an hour later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you go to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there. I had a lot of friends there. It wasn't very nice in Grabovica. It was dirty and it wasn't really very nice. The accommodation was bad. Like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you stay in Jablanica through the night?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The -- did you return to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you returned, did you return in the morning, noontime, or in the afternoon, or evening?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you returned, did you hear something from the other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that somebody had killed these civilians in Grabovica, and I heard that Ramiz Delalic brought two boys, that he lined up the unit, and brought those two young boys to recognise -- he lined them up to see if they could recognise who had killed their parents. That's what I heard. I didn't -- I wasn't there during this line-up, but this is what I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you see any corpses or dead bodies when you returned to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anything on the roadway or in the buildings which could have been the remains or -- could have been the remains of any of these corpses or any blood or something that looked like blood?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In one section of the road, I saw a kind of puddle, like blood or paint, but it was very, very faint. You could hardly notice it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, was there any combat activities occurring in the village of Grabovica during your stay there?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear of any combat activities in Grabovica during the time that you stayed in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear or did you see any Croatian soldiers in Grabovica while you were there?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after this date, did you eventually enter some combat action?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After which date?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'll make it easier. Were you eventually sent into combat action?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Where did they send you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the Vrdi village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've testified previously that you returned, which would have been on September 10th, and you learnt about some deaths occurring in Grabovica. In relation to that, when in relation to that date were you sent into combat action?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was on the third night, on the 10th in the evening at around 11.00 p.m. Before midnight. We left Grabovica for Dreznica before midnight, around 11.00, to go to Vrdi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you sent into combat action in Vrdi?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that -- or actually, how long did the combat action last?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We set off at about 11.00 in the evening. We travelled on foot that night. In the morning, we started to go up the mountain, to Vrdi, and we returned in the evening when it was dark. And we stayed -- okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just ask you a couple quick questions: Did you return to Grabovica after Vrdi?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go next? You said you went someplace in the mountains?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We returned from that operation to some village above Dreznica. I don't remember any more what the name of the village was, but it was a small one with just a few houses, a couple of houses. We spent the night there, and the next day we went to Medved Mountain to another operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you eventually return to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we returned from Mount Medved, yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, there is. Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Morrissey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mehanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit P7.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Mehanovic, I'm going to ask you to mark this picture as well. Mr. Mehanovic, you indicated that when Mr. Karic was present, that the soldiers were in three columns. Could you please draw with lines the three columns that you say the soldiers were in.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if it was two, three, or four, but in any case -- I don't know how many soldiers there were, but the space from the house to the road here was filled. So it would be something like that, from here to here. Like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Well, that single line -- were the three -- two, three, or four columns -- could you draw a second column in relation to that first one, please.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One column was behind the other. I can't really tell you exactly, but this is approximately what it looked like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. Very well. Now, could you just write the number "1" underneath those lines to indicate that those lines are the soldiers. Just write the numeral "1".

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And put a circle around that numeral "1", please.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, to indicate where you say the Croatian civilian was standing, could you draw a circle and put the number "2" inside that.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please draw a cross to show where Mr. Karic was standing.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please draw -- and could you write the number "3" next to that cross, on the left-hand side, inside a circle.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please draw a number "4" to indicate approximately where you say Sefer Halilovic was at the time Karic made the comment.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please draw a circle with a number "5" to indicate where you say Zuka, Zulfikar Alispago, was at the time that that comment was made.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less they were next to each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, at the time when Mr. Karic made the comment that you've related to the Court, Halilovic and Alispago were both engaged in speaking to the troops; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And according to you, the comment made by Karic was made in a normal conversational voice and not shouting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, Karic was engaged in speaking to an individual soldier who had made a complaint; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it now too many years ago for you to remember the name of that particular soldier who made the complaint?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand if the witness said yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not just one. Practically all of them were complaining.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But I'm talking about the specific conversation that was going on between Karic and the individual soldier that I've just spoken to you about. Can you remember the name of that soldier that Karic was speaking to?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That soldier you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now -- we've got up to number 5. Would you now mark approximately with a number "6" whereabouts you were when Mr. Karic made the comment.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. At the beginning. More or less at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. Doing the best you can, can you put a number "7", please, at where Mr. Elvedin Husic was.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot do that because I don't know where he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he between you and Mr. Karic or not?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I offer that document for tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess there's no objections from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It's admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Defence Exhibit D175.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mehanovic, I have some preliminary questions relating to the time before the Grabovica incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the fact that you joined a -- sorry, I'll start this question again. The 9th Brigade evolved out of pre-existing army units in Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the 3rd and 7th Mountain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Did you join the 7th Mountain Brigade on the 22nd of July, 1992 at the same time as Elvedin Husic and four other individuals whose names I'll give to you if you need them? But really I'm interested in the date. So did you join the brigade on the 22nd of the -- of July, 1992 with Elvedin Husic?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which brigade?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the 3rd Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I don't know exactly the date, but it was July or August. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm just going to show you a document now, if I could, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document has only just been translated. It's not in the system. This is another act against the e-court. It's just been done now. We'll provide copies in all relevant languages and, of course, provide it for the e-court to be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be marked for identification 176.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I'm grateful for the court staff to remind me. That's marked for identification 176 at this stage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just -- you can take your time to read that, but I'll ask you some questions while you're looking at it and perhaps you can answer them as we go along. Would you look first of all at the signature on this document. It's at the bottom of the second page. Do you see that signature there? The bottom right of the second page.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is that, as far as you know, the signature of Tomislav Juric, who ultimately became the chief of military security in the 9th Brigade in 1993?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if that is his signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you for an expert opinion on his signature, but -- well, perhaps I should ask you this: You know Tomislav -- or you knew Tomislav Juric at the time?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he held the position I just indicated, chief of security -- of military security in the 9th Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Would you mind now just going back to the -- to the first page. And I just want to -- to note a couple of details of that. First of all, six names from the -- or five names from the bottom, do you see the name Nedzad Mehanovic?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you can see the address there, 22nd -- sorry, the date there, 22nd of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you acknowledge that that's correct, that in fact you did join that unit, that being the predecessor to the 9th Brigade, the 3rd Mountain Brigade, on that date?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't, because I don't know for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Would you turn over the page, please. And do you see where the list of names comes to an end over the page? Six names from the bottom there, the name Husic Elvedin?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you join on the same day as Husic Elvedin?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Well, I offer that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: For whatever it's worth, Your Honour, he can -- he can't authenticate it and -- for whatever weight the Court wants to give it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's -- the matter can be debated at the end of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I simply offer it at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm not objecting to it, but for whatever little weight it's worth. What it's worth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, of course, you know, if you want to tender this document, you have to lay some foundations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If you could do it at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps just to conclude, then, in respect to this document here, you're familiar with many of the names on that document, including Hukelic Ertan, Kajevic Fikret? You know those names?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Fikret Kajevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know Erdin Arnautovic?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Ertan Hukelic?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Kemo Kapur?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Mustafa Hota?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you notice there the date next to the name of the Mustafa Hota? It says 15/9/93. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. To your knowledge, Mustafa Hota arrived in the 9th Brigade in July of 1993. In other words, only a month or so before the action in Herzegovina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm putting to you is that he arrived in the -- in the 9th Brigade on the 15th of July of 1993 and was only formally accepted into the brigade on the 15th of September, 1993. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when he was formally accepted, but I believe that in 1993, maybe it was April or May when he joined us, but it was certainly before June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was after your trip to Jablanica in the springtime, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. Maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. Have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I'm going to move on to some questions about what occurred in Sarajevo. You, like the other troops, lined up at the 9th Brigade headquarters when Vahid Karavelic, commander of the 1st Corps, came and spoke to you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after receiving orders from Karavelic and after a short delay, you set off through the tunnel to meet some trucks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on your way down to Jablanica, present with you was your commander, Ramiz Delalic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were on the truck with Mr. Elvedin Husic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it's the fact, isn't it, that you were at that time friends with Elvedin Husic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And even since the war stopped, you remained friends with Elvedin Husic; is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry, Mr. Mehanovic. The question I asked you was: You've remained friends with Elvedin Husic since the war ended; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Upon arrival at Jablanica, your commander, Ramiz Delalic, was still present with the unit for at least some time of your stop in Jablanica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Donja Jablanica. He stayed in Donja Jablanica in Zuka's base, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you're correct to correct me. It was in fact -- well, it's the fact that your unit arrived with Ramiz Delalic at Donja Jablanica and stopped there for a period of time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 15, 20 minutes approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that 15 to 20 minutes, you saw personally Zulfikar Alispago, the commander of the unit that was called Zuka's Unit; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment when we arrived you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, within that period of time, that 15, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you see Zuka in that time or not?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I can't say one way or another with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Zuka's -- I'm sorry, I've slipped into using of nicknames there. Did you see Zulfikar Alispago's commander of logistics, a man who went by the name of Spaga?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Spaga a man aged between 30 and 40 with brown hair? Sorry, I'll ask that question again: Was at that time Spaga a man aged between 30 and 40 with brown-coloured hair?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I think he was older than 40, I would say. I -- as far as I know, his name is Nedzad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the name Spaga that I mentioned to you, was that a nickname or a real name?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a nickname, Spago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Do you know the full name of Nedzad, who had the nickname Spago?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used to know, but it eludes me now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Is it a long time since you saw that person?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, as you indicated to the Prosecutor, you had personally been in Jablanica before in approximately May of 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April. Just excuse me one moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that time, you indicated to my learned friend Mr. Weiner, the Prosecutor, that you became involved in some fighting down there at an early stage in the fighting between the Bosnian army and the HVO. And what I want to ask you is: Were there any other 9th Brigade soldiers who helped in that fighting in April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when we came out to get those weapons and uniforms, Fikret Fajovic [phoen], Fadil Kurgas, and I believe Sato Koca were with me. I'm not sure. Safet Koca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to your recollection, a small detachment of the 9th Brigade fought in Herzegovina in April of 1993 already; is that true?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not a small detachment. It was just the four of us. In fact, even Fikret was not there. He left two or three days later. I was left with Fadil and Safet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during that time, did you come to be arrested by the local military police for being in possession of 19 bottles of good-quality Bacardi rum?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not arrest me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did they take you in for questioning concerning the possession of 19 bottles of Bacardi rum at that time?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not take me into custody. They just invited me for an interview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did you oblige them by attending for that interview?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And was the substance of the allegation -- and Mr. Mehanovic, I'm not going to put every detail of it, but in general terms was the substance of the allegation this, that found in your hotel room --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. These charges did not result in an arrest, do not result in a conviction, and are irrelevant to the charges against this defendant. You could impeach him with a prior conviction, a prior -- which would constitute a prior bad act. But when a person is questioned about something, it's irrelevant and not worthy of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that in the cross-examination the Defence team could ask any questions which might challenge the credibility of a particular witness. Am I right, Mr. Morrissey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Or you mean -- you mean that incident has something to do with --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's got something to do with the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: With the case?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Which happened in --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Which I haven't got to yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's fair, Your Honour. I withdraw it. That's fair. If he can tie it to the case, I withdraw my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. And maybe it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Or maybe you could finish that part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I could just finish that part. It's not very long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In five minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Oh, easily. Easily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Mehanovic. Just so as to be fair with you, the fact is you were never charged with this -- this incident once the police questioning had taken place; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was no reason for charges to be pressed, because it wasn't I who did it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. But what happened was that 19 bottles of Bacardi rum were found in your hotel room; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But -- yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In fact, Your Honour, that's as far as that part of the questioning has to go, and I'm ready for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take 30 minutes' break, and we'll resume at ten minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mehanovic, having arrived at Jablanica, according to you Ramiz Delalic did not go on to the village of Grabovica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And neither did Malco Rovcanin go on to Grabovica; is that correct too?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it from that that as the troops arrived in -- in Grabovica, there was effectively no one in command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. All I know is that two, three, or maybe even four men out of Zuka's logistics unit came with us to show us where we would be staying, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But it's not the tradition to follow the orders of logistics men, is it, Mr. Mehanovic?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. But we were under Zulfikar Alispago's command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. But Zulfikar Alispago was not with you, was he?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I just want to be clear about this. There was a -- an occasion in 1999, on the 11th of November, 1999, when you made a statement to investigators from this Tribunal. And at page 3 there, you said this- and I'll ask you to confirm whether it's accurate or not once I've read it out to you. Okay? Now I'm quoting: "I cannot give a description of Zuka's men" -- well, in fairness to you, Mr. Mehanovic. I'm just going to read the bit before. It will make more sense. "Zuka's men told us that we would have a rest in that courtyard and would then be sent to houses in which we were to stay. I cannot give a description of Zuka's men. We stayed in that courtyard for about 30 minutes. I'm sure that I remember them showing our soldiers the houses in the village in which they were to stay. One of them showed us the house which was situated in the middle of the village. The house was vacant. There were about four or five of us who entered that house, including Haris Salihovic, a man called Crni, Regan, Suljo, and one other person. Haris was from my platoon and the others were from the engineer platoon. As far as I remember, no commander was appointed to be in charge of the soldiers of the 9th Brigade during our stay in Grabovica." Now, Mr. Mehanovic, I know that that was quite a lengthy quote to read out but I just wanted to give you the full context. Do you agree with that, that that's true, that -- as far as you remember, no commander was appointed to be in charge of the soldiers of the 9th Brigade during your stay in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, I want to take you to the journey from Jablanica down to Grabovica. On that journey, you were escorted by the approximately four of Zuka's logistics soldiers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once again, the individual Spaga was present.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if he went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Upon arrival at Grabovica, you were accommodated in houses without any trouble at all; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the house where I was staying, there was first Crni, Regan, and Suljo. Myself and Haris came to that house in the evening just before dark, or maybe it was late afternoon. We stayed for 30, maybe 60 minutes, and then we went on to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Well, I'm going to read to you a passage from a record of a witness hearing compiled on the 12th of January, 1999 at the cantonal court in front of the investigative judge Ibrahim Hadzic. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And this, Your Honours is at page 3, at the top of page 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said this: "Together with three other soldiers, engineers from our company, Crni, Regan, and one more person whose name I can't remember now, got accommodation in an abandoned house. We had no trouble with the accommodation. Other soldiers from our company were accommodated in surrounding houses." Now, having said that to the cantonal court judge -- well, perhaps I should ask you this: Did you say that to the cantonal court judge and is that the truth?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still say when Haris and I came to that house, Crni, Regan, and Suljo were already there and they told us there were no civilians inside or around, and I didn't see any civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Out of those -- but just -- I understand you say that, and what I'm really asking you is to confirm what you said to the judge at the cantonal court that there was no trouble with accommodation; in other words, "We had no trouble with the accommodation." Is that the truth?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in that house, because there was nobody there. It was empty. Well, I don't know what he wrote and how he explained it, but I'm telling you just as I would be -- as if -- if I were talking to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Now, is your position this: That you didn't see any civilians during your stay in the -- in the village of Grabovica? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw civilians, but I didn't see any in that house where I was billeted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. I want to put something to you from the very same statement to the cantonal court. Okay? You just have to excuse me one moment, please. This is in the middle of page 3, Your Honour. And you said this: "After the second or the third night, I have heard about the killing of some civilians in Grabovica. This was heard from the soldiers who started talking. I heard about the killing of these civilians when we were getting food rations from Zuka's Unit. At the place we were meeting to get the food and take it back to where we were staying there were soldiers from whom I heard that some civilians were killed. I cannot remember exactly who told me that, but the soldiers were talking about it among themselves. For the time I spent in the village, I did not see or contact any civilians and I did not see the murdered civilians about whose murder was talked about." Now, is that true that for the time you spent in the village, you did not see or contact any civilians and did not see the murdered civilians whose murder was discussed?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is all so, except for seeing that man on the balcony when we were lined up. I saw that man on the balcony. I didn't see any of the others or the -- didn't have any contact with them. And I didn't see them being killed either, and I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You just have to excuse me one moment, please, Mr. Mehanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mehanovic, I'm going to put something to you from -- a statement given by you and provided to us by the Prosecutor. This statement is dated the 23rd of March, 1998. And in this statement, at the bottom of page 1, if it pleases the Court, did you say this: "Of the people who were accommodated together with me in the same house, I can remember a certain Crni and Regan, members of the engineer's battalion. Now, was that true?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "I noticed that a large number of civilians were in the village and I found out that they were of Croatian nationality." Now, is that true?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who wrote that. Listen, a large number of civilians? There were only a few -- a couple of houses there. They were of Croat ethnicity, but I don't believe that I said that it was a large number, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Well, did you sign this statement following reading the words at the end of it, saying: "Statement given by Nedzad Mehanovic, statement taken by Zlatko Prndelj and countersigned by Fadil Zolota on the 23rd of the third, 1998? Did you sign that statement or not?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is at the MUP; right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did sign it. But I didn't write what I signed, because I never need to read it back. I know what I say. It's the same as what they put there, that I was drinking alcohol. These are just games of theirs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just a moment, Mr. -- Mr. Mehanovic. You've been in police stations on a number of occasions in your career, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For example, when you were in the police station -- or the military police station in Jablanica back in 1993 in April, you had suggestions and questions put to you by the police on that occasion and you felt free to deny them in accordance with the truth; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't with the military police but at the MUP, the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, what I'm putting to you is that you don't sign something unless you know it's true; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I say, I expect them to also note down. But it happened that the investigator Nikolai -- there is 90 per cent of untruths there. I don't speak in the way that it's recorded in that statement. There's at least 90 per cent of untruths in that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I'm not asking you about Nikolai right now, Mr. Mehanovic, but about your trip to the MUP and the statement which you signed at the MUP. Now, when you signed that statement at the MUP, there was no question of that being translated into the English language, was there? It was all done in Bosnian; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you can read and write, can't you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And you know that sometimes the police might try to slip in an occasional extra fact into a statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if it suits them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. So you read this statement very carefully before you signed it, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, can I suggest to you it's a certainty because you are very careful about what you sign in police stations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that I'm careful. I sign it. But I don't understand what I read back, because I know what I was saying, for today and even in a hundred year's time if necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Mr. Mehanovic, I don't want to fight with you unnecessarily over this, but it's a matter I'm going to press you about. I'll give you an example. You recall being questioned in relation to a rape in the year 1997? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that occasion, you knew that there was an allegation being made against you that you'd taken a girl in your employment and driven her to a dark back street in Bembasa Street, and you'd attempted to rape her in your car; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, unless there is an arrest, unless there is a conviction, a certified copy of a conviction, such evidence is not admissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, and this allegation also related to the privacy of the matters, not only to this witness but also to others.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, to deal with the second point that Your Honour has just raised there, I wasn't proposing to name the individual, if the name looks like coming up, we can go into the private session. Is -- was that Your Honour's concern on that matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, this is just one part. I just want to know whether it's absolutely necessary for you to use this incident to impeach this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, it's really about, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I -- I understand that, but it seems to me that you have already made your point there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And I believe that's enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. We may move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, but I have one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I explain about this girl that the gentleman is talking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, witness, I think the Defence team has agreed that we skip that part and we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it shouldn't end just on that because -- all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. Yes, you may move on, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, what do you say about this? You've signed a statement where you've said, "I noticed a large number of civilians," but your account to this Court now is quite different. You're saying that you didn't see any, except of course for the lonely Croat on the balcony. So --

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's the -- the need for the change, Mr. Mehanovic?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What change?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The change from no -- from many civilians to no civilians.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that I said that about many civilians, because that is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown photograph number 79, P79.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mehanovic, while this is done, I'm going to ask you some -- to mark another photograph, a large panoramic photograph. Do you have in front of you now a photograph which has got a large number of yellow arrows on it?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. Mr. Mehanovic, just go to the left-hand side of the photograph and notice there on the left-hand end the meadow where you say the line-up took place where Mr. Karic said the words that you've ascribed to him. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you see there the white house without a roof which was shown in the previous photograph that you looked at earlier on?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you also see in the trees there the house on which you say the -- the lonely Croat was standing at the time of Mr. Karic's words?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I'm going to ask you now to locate certain individuals within the village. First of all, would you please mark with a circle and a number "1" the house in which you, Crni, and Regan found yourselves.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was Crni's real name Mr. Turkovic?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Last name, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Would you now, please, mark with a number "2" the house where Nihad Vlahovljak and his soldiers were located.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I don't know. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you to look at that blue woodsmoke which can be seen in the middle left of the photograph. Do you see that blue woodsmoke?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your recollection, was Vlahovljak and his team located in a farmhouse somewhere in that area?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever visit Mr. Vlahovljak and his team during your stay in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please mark the house at which Erdin Arnautovic, the logistics man from the 9th Brigade, took up his residence in the village, with a number "2".

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where he was, in which house. All I know that -- is that Adnan Solakovic was in this one down here, actually his soldiers, in this first one down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you --

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the rest, I don't know where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We'll take it step by step. Please mark with a number "2" now the house where the Solakovic soldiers were.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you a question: As you come into the village from Jablanica, the house where the Solakovic soldiers are, according to you, is almost the last house in the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that. There's another one up there. What do I know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you would deny any suggestion that the Solakovic soldiers were in fact billeted in the house that you've marked as yours, house number 1; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in this house which I circled and marked with the number "1", and I know that they were over there. There's nothing for me to deny. I don't know what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please mark with a number "3" the house where your friend, Elvedin Husic, was accommodated.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I have no idea who was staying where. I know where I was billeted, and I happen to know where Solakovic's soldiers were because they arrived at Grabovica before us. I don't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But Mr. Mehanovic, Mr. Husic was your friend. Surely you must have visited him during your stay in the village.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
