utterances.text: What does that have to do with anything? He wasn't my wife or anything like that. I didn't have to know where he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you may not have had to have known where he was, but what I'm putting to you fair and square is you did know where he was and I'm asking you now to exercise your memory and to tell us. Can you do that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I'm telling you that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a checkpoint set up when you arrived on the 8th anywhere in the village?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not when we arrived, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the first checkpoint appear in the village, to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that it was set up after the killings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whereabouts -- did you ever see that checkpoint yourself with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came back to the village after Ramiz Delalic performed the line-up, did you notice a checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there for the line-up, and as I said, I didn't notice the checkpoint. Actually, I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, checkpoints being checkpoints, Mr. Mehanovic, I suppose what you're saying is you didn't get stopped at a checkpoint when you came back; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I didn't see it when I came. When I returned, it was approximately on the 9th or the 10th in the afternoon. That's when I came back. And it wasn't there then, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The final question about that is: I want you to indicate on that map with a "3" the location of the house where Musa Hota was accommodated.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know anyone in the 9th Brigade with the nickname Tiki, Grga, or Kralj - I'll spell those as they appeared. Tiki is T-i-k-i; Grga, G-r-g-a; and Kralj, K-r-a-l-j.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm hearing those nicknames for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you're concerned, no people with those nicknames were part of the 9th Brigade during your time in Grabovica or indeed at any other time?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I am hearing those nicknames for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I offer that diagram.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess there's no objections? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The photograph will be marked Defence Exhibit D177.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that. Thank you. I'm grateful for that indication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I've now got some questions for you concerning the visit of Mr. Karic which you've described taking place. On that occasion, did you see a man called Huso Alic, with the nickname Soko, who was an officer from Zuka's Unit?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know him. I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see on that occasion when you saw the lonely Croat and Karic speaking, a man called Rifat Bilajac.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of him. But I think I don't know him. I don't know what he looks like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see on that occasion a man called Zicro Suljevic?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about a security officer on that occasion named Namik Dzankovic? Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know him either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've got some questions for you about what you saw. I'm not going to ask you again about the words that you ascribed to Mr. Karic. But I do want to ask you about this man on the balcony. How long was he on the balcony?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was present all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On how many other occasions have you noticed senior commanders to address their troops about an upcoming operation in the presence of a civilian whose ethnicity is connected to the other team?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't suggest that Karic told that Croatian man to go inside or go away, do you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't say anything to him in that sense. Or at least I didn't hear it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you were right there, according to you; correct? Merely two or three metres away.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I just want to ask you -- I'm going to ask you a number of questions about this, but I just want to ask you one: Is it possible that you have become confused in your memory that Sefer Halilovic was there at all on this occasion? Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean to say there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in court now many years later, you say you remember Halilovic being present and talking to soldiers at the other end of the line when Mr. Karic made these comments. But I want to ask you: Is it possible that you've made a mistake and that Sefer Halilovic just wasn't there on that day at all? Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't make a mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me read to you from the statement that I've already put to you dated the 23rd of the 3rd, 1998, which you've acknowledged signing, and this is on page 2 of that statement: "I think we had already spent two days in Grabovica when Vehbija Karic arrived in the village with his associates. I was there when -- while Vehbija Karic and our commanders were making a plan about reconnaissance of the enemy positions. Somebody amongst the persons present complained about some of the civilians of Croatian nationality making problems with regard to accommodation of soldiers in the houses of Grabovica. Vehbija Karic went mad and said loudly, 'you know what to do with them. Make it short and swift.' I spent that evening at home, where I drank alcoholic drinks with my room-mates." Now, do you agree with me the --

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wait for a moment, please. The Prosecutor can correct me if there's any difficulties with what I put. Do you agree with me that nowhere in that statement did you mention once the name Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, in each statement I said the same thing, just as I stated it now. As for who wrote down what, that is something that I'm not interested in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. Well, there's three matters I want to put to you from this statement just to see whether you -- whether you accept them as true or say that they're false: Firstly, it says here, "I think we've already spent two days in Grabovica when Vehbija Karic arrived." Now, is that true or is that false?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only Vehbija Karic arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next thing that I want to ask you about is that there's no mention in this statement at all of you returning to Jablanica. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After half an hour or an hour when that meeting ended, I went to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's the reason you didn't say that when speaking to the police and signing the statement that we now are putting to you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I said that for sure, but as far as what they wrote down, I'm not interested in that. I was never interested in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you say, "I spent that evening at home where I drank alcoholic drinks with my room-mates"?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you say it though?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say it like that, because I wasn't drinking. There is no alcohol there. How could there be any alcohol in Grabovica? As far as the things that they wrote down, I had nothing to do with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And is there a reason therefore why you signed this document here, relatively short document, written in Bosnian, which contained these things which you now say are false?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're driving at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm driving at -- just so that you're not under any misapprehension, I'm driving that you've changed your story on a number of occasions which I'm going to put to you. Do you fully understand that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am telling you that I said the same thing then as I'm saying now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In fact, Your Honours, given that the witness has accepted signing that document, I seek to tender that document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, I would object, Your Honour, unless we're going to tender all prior documents in of prior inconsistent statements. As the Court knows, in this jurisdiction -- or I'm sorry, before this Court, prior inconsistent statements come in orally through testimony. The documents themselves are not admissible. If you want to see the Strugar decision, I believe it's number 3 on the admissibility of evidence 2004, it indicates that such evidence based on the policy of this Tribunal is not admissible at trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I think on that point, I agree with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we also noticed that you used very extensively the part of that document already and everything you said is registered in the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the Court pleases. Yes, I won't seek to press it further than I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mehanovic. Now, your claim here in court is that the Karic incident happens the day after you arrive; that's correct, isn't it? Or do you say it's on the day that you arrive?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where did you stay the first night that you were present in the village? In Jablanica or in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is your position this: That you arrived with the troops on the 8th; that you then went to Jablanica for the night of the 8th; that you came back on the next day, and that's when the Karic village -- visit took place to the village?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So -- and you're not making this up as you go along, are you, Mr. Mehanovic? That's what you remember; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object, Your Honour. Argumentative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is very argumentative.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, actually, Your Honour, it was meant to be positively fawning and agreeing, as Your Honour will see from the question. I put to him he's not making it up, that he's giving proper evidence about this, and that that's the case. But if my friend has a difficulty with it, it's icing on the cake twice, Your Honour. I withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yeah. I believe that the witness has already answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: He has. He has.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what that means anyway, to be quite clear, is that you arrive on the 8th and Mr. Karic arrives on the 9th; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your meeting with Mr. Karic took place -- I think you've indicated that is it was sometime in the afternoon. Do you mean around the end of the afternoon, say 5.30 in the evening, or do you mean mid-afternoon, around 3.00, or perhaps at about 3.30 or 4.00, or do you mean very early afternoon?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. I'll try it another way. You've indicated that you heard that Mr. Karic was coming at lunchtime. You recall that? When you were given your lunch packets.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. It was not only Karic. I repeat again: It was that officers from the General Staff were supposed to come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Well, what I'm getting at here is the timing factor now. You got that news at lunchtime and then a couple of hours passed before they came. Is that accurate or wrong?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came around 2.00, 2.30, maybe 3.00. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I won't try to lock you to a specific time, but what you're saying is mid-afternoon, around the 2.30 to 3.00 mark; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear any shooting going on while the soldiers were lined up?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any livestock being driven around by soldiers at that time?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you glance to the left bank of the village and see elderly Croatian civilians fleeing the village on foot along the road to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any police vehicles attending on the right bank and stopping near to the house which you say you were accommodated in?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear the screams of any frightened civilians?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get into -- well, I'm going to go back to the 8th now, the day of your arrival, okay? And I think you've indicated there that you ultimately came to the house that you occupied at about 5.00 approximately; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, late afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between the time you arrived at the village and entering the house that you entered, did you hear any shooting or guns going off?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear the distressed screams of any civilians?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I think, Mr. Mehanovic, you understand what I'm asking, and what I'm asking you is this: Are you up to your neck in the killing of these civilians yourself?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In fact, I don't quite understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you left about half an hour after arriving at your house. And I want to ask you: Was it light or dark when you left to go to Jablanica on the night of the 8th?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was light. It was summertime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get into Jablanica? Did you have a vehicle or a bicycle or did you go on foot?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We stopped some kind of jeep or van or something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean you stopped some kind of jeep or van? Do you mean a jeep or van that just happened to be passing by, or a jeep or van owned and operated by the soldiers in the village?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not from the village. It just came by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It came by on the main road, according to you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was on the main road. This jeep or van was just passing by on the main road from Mostar to Jablanica. It was not from the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as -- therefore, as you left the right bank village, you had to walk out along that track and cross over the iron bridge to get to the main road; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which railroad? There is no railroad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, it's okay. My words have led you astray. I mean the path - the road, not the railroad, but the road - which leaves the village and rejoins the main highway. What I'm putting to you is: In order to get to the highway, you had to go along that road and cross over an iron bridge. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were you with when you crossed over that iron bridge?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Haris, this friend of mine, and I.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't get on a bicycle with a man named Mr. Turkovic, Crni, did you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Where would we get a bicycle there? We certainly didn't take one from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the Croatian civilians while they were alive own bicycles?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me put another question to you: Did you go into Jablanica and buy some alcohol for the troops?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know, don't you, that Ramiz Delalic when he was present would not tolerate the drinking of alcohol by the troops; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But Ramiz Delalic wasn't present, was he, on the night of the 8th in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you had been and your unit had been stuck in Sarajevo in siege conditions for -- I withdraw that. I'll put another question. You had been fighting hard battles in Sarajevo and on Igman for weeks, if not months, before this trip to Herzegovina; is that true?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whilst I'm not suggesting that it was in the least a holiday to go to Herzegovina to fight in a war, you and the other soldiers did look forward to getting out of Sarajevo for a while; is that true?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you arrived at Grabovica, the commander was missing; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, he was off in Jablanica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Zuka was our commander. That's how the Karavelic read the order to us. As soon as we cross the runway, Zuka was supposed to take over command. That's how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fairness to you, that is what you said earlier. But my question is a bit different. What I'm putting to you is here you were in Herzegovina with no one supervising you in the village. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is something I don't know. That's a question you'd better ask the people from the Supreme Command. It's not my level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm asking you about is how alcohol got to that village. Can you answer that question? How did alcohol come to be in that village?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It's the first time now that I hear from you that there were any vehicles there -- there was -- sorry, there was alcohol.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter misunderstood. That there was any alcohol there at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You certainly knew where to find alcohol in Jablanica, didn't you, Mr. Mehanovic?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What alcohol are you talking about? Are you trying to make out that I was an alcoholic or something?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm trying to put to you that you went -- well, I'm not putting it to you but I'm querying with you whether you went and collected alcohol from Jablanica, given your contacts at Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't -- I didn't go and get alcohol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, what you'd say is according to you, on the 8th of -- on the 8th of September, you heard no guns, no screams, and in short nothing to cause you to think that anything was wrong at all whilst you were in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object, Your Honour. That's argumentative and it's also asked and answered previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I believe this question has been raised and answered already.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when you got to Jablanica, where did you go on the night of the 8th?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Jablanica. Where could I go?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm asking you. Did you go to a friend's house?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we did go around town, cafes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you end up, in terms of sleeping?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which hotel?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Jablanica Hotel. There's only one hotel, as far as I know. Maybe they've built some more since then, but at that time there was only one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether members of the Security Services were billeted in that hotel at that time?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about a man called Brankovic? Was he billeted in that hotel at that time?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Namik Dzankovic?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How big a hotel is the Jablanica Hotel?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's a two-storey, maybe a three-storey building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the book?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any of Mr. Suljevic, Bilajac, or Karic at the hotel that night when you went to stay there?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time did you leave to go back to Grabovica the next morning?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you arrive back in Grabovica at about 11.30, say half past 11.00 to 12.00, late in the morning on the 9th of September?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, around 11.00, 12.00. I'm not sure. It was before lunch, in any case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you pass by a man called Marinko Dreznjak as he fled from the village down that road?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you run into a refugee -- a Muslim refugee woman called Munevera Repesa present on the right bank with her daughter?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that we go into the private session for the reasons indicated earlier on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mehanovic. Did you tell the cantonal court in -- I'll give row the date of it -- on the 12th of January -- just excuse me a moment. I just want to make sure that the date has been correctly put here. Yes, did you tell the cantonal court in a record of the hearing of the witness compiled on the 12th of the January, 1999, which has been provided by the Prosecution to the Defence and is to be found at page 3, Your Honours, about ten lines from the top -- did you tell the cantonal court this: "I would like to emphasise that I came to an abandoned house where there were no civilians, and I would also like to point out that I did not notice any civilians at all. I know that we spent the first night there as well as the second night. However, after the second or third night, I have heard about the killing of some civilians in Grabovica." Now, is that what you told the cantonal court in Sarajevo and is it true?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that and it's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the story of your trip to Jablanica a relatively recent invention invented sometime after the evidence that you gave to the cantonal court?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object, Your Honour. That's an argument. That's not a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that you have raised this question already, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I raised that specific one, but I think I have to in fairness put it to the witness. I don't want to be criticised at a later time for failing to give the witness an opportunity to comment on the grave allegations that we're going to make and are making now. If the Prosecution says that they won't make that point, then that's the end of that question. If they don't say that and if they don't agree with Your Honour's summary, then I'd seem to persist with the question. And could we ask Mr. Weiner what his position is about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The question -- I mean, he can -- he can question in that area, but the form of the question itself is argumentative. It's a summary. It's not a question that's admissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Morrissey, you may show some, you know, documents or previous statement to this witness before that, in that in the past you didn't mention this issue but now suddenly we hear --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- you know, you are talking about your trip to Jablanica. Why is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, that's what the thrust of the question was. I agree to ask it that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mehanovic, can you point to any document where you make the claim of going to Jablanica on the first night prior to the year of 1999?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you show me that I did not go to Jablanica? Can you demonstrate that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you another question: You've been around the criminal justice system a while, haven't you, Mr. Mehanovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that's not a proper comment, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I withdraw it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I'll press on with something that concerns us with the case. Let me just ask you another question: Are you concerned in your evidence here to protect any person from exposure to criminal prosecutions in the new war crimes Chamber in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean. I'm telling you what I know and what I saw. Whether I will protect anybody or inflict damage on anyone with that, I don't know. I'm just saying what I saw and what I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mehanovic, I've got to ask you about a police case in 1997. It's not the one we referred to earlier. It's a different one. Mr. Mehanovic, were you indicted in 1997 for an event involving a display of force in a restaurant in Bembasa Street following the finding of three hand grenades at your apartment? Were you indicted by that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Once again, Your Honour, I object. How is any of this admissible? If they have a certified copy of a conviction or if they have some sort of conviction, that you can question a person about. But we're just talking about a charge, an interview, an investigation, an indictment. Without a conviction, questioning should not be allowed. It's irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, it's directly relevant to relationship evidence, Your Honour. It's got nothing to do with impugning his credit. And in fact, I'm going to lead from him that he was never convicted of this. But it's got to do with other matters and I would seek to persist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that this question is allowed. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you recall being indicted for that incident in 1997? Mr. Mehanovic, would it assist if I showed you a copy of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I -- this is another matter that's only just been translated, and I would seek that -- I'm sorry to do this, but I'm running against the clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are waiting for the answer from this witness. If there's no doubts about that, why should we have this indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, what is it, witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time that I'm hearing of anything like this. First of all, no bombs were thrown at my apartment, and I am hearing for the first time that I am being charged for something like that. Could you please show us that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness please be shown the indictment that is about to be shown. Would Your Honour just excuse me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just excuse us a moment, Mr. Mehanovic, and we'll provide everyone in the court with what you need and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think Your Honours and, Mr. Prosecutor, I think what you have should be a three-page indictment and then a translation of that following it in English. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you see there the fourth name on that list is the name -- on that indictment is the name Nedzad Mehanovic?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The nickname of Necko?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it gives details, including occupation, caterer, and other details which we don't need to go into? Okay? Do you see all that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not concerned with asking you about your guilt or innocence of that particular matter at this stage. Okay? But do you recall being charged -- being indicted under this indictment now that you're looking at?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wait a minute.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time that I'm seeing this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry? You've never seen the indictment?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall seeing it, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You recall though -- just bear with me for a moment, please. You recall, don't you, that you were spoken to by police concerning the finding of three M-93 hand grenades in your apartment during a police search? You recall being questioned about that matter?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I don't need to know any details of what you told your lawyer at the time, but you spoke to a lawyer about these allegations against you, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably did. I don't know. Oh, these are three -- the three bombs that -- the hand grenades that stayed -- that I had left from the war. I think that's written down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, as I said to you, I'm not concerned to try to make you get found guilty of that now. Do you follow that -- in fact, I'll ask you this question: To your knowledge, in 1993 [sic] the prosecution against you was discontinued because it ran out of time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This says 1997. He just mentioned 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And why is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's an error. 2003. I apologise. The reason it's relevant, could I just indicate, is because I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No. Wait. Wait. Wait. Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Once again, why is this relevant?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Morrissey maybe could show us the relevance of this to our present case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. That last question there has very limited relevance, but it was designed to be fair to the witness so that he doesn't think that it's being suggested that he was guilty. I'm just putting to him at the moment that he was charged, and that's why I was putting that to him, that the charge didn't go any further, so as not to mislead him or the Court into thinking that it was being put to credit. It's not being put to credit. But, Your Honours, I agree -- I won't put the question, and if my friend thinks it's irrelevant, I just won't put it. I agree. I withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm not talking just about the question but this whole line of questioning. How is this relevant?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, the next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Me too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could show us?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In one question I'll show you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see who's the first named person on that indictment there?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. [Previous translation continues] ... is your co-accused in the 1997 matter Ramiz Delalic?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really -- it doesn't state here that I was there at all. I don't know how it is that I ended up on that list. As far as I am able to read, it doesn't say here at all that I participated or that I was with him, on the first page. My name is not mentioned at all, that I was with him at all. Whether they were there or not is something that I really don't know and I'm not interested in it either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm putting to you is this: You were a co-accused of Ramiz Delalic in 1997. Do you agree with me? I'm not saying you were guilty or that he was guilty. And, in fact, neither of you got found guilty. But I'm asking you to acknowledge this: That the authorities jointly accused you and Ramiz at the same time on the same indictment. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I was indicted because of these three hand grenades that were found in my apartment, for unlawful possession of weapons and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I offer that document for tender.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: On what basis, Your Honour? To show what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's being led to show a relationship between this man and Ramiz Delalic at a time later. It's directly relevant to issues of the construction of the statement. It's directly relevant to matters I'm going to rely on at a later time. I'm going to put it to Mr. -- to another witness who's being referred to elsewhere when he comes. And if this witness -- I'm sorry, I take that back. But if anyone else mentioned in this indictment should chance to appear -- Well, could I move into the private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this stage we would like to hold the admission of this document for a while. If in the future you could show more relevance to this case, we will have it admitted. Otherwise --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But anyway, we should give a number to that document for the future, you know, usage. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will exhaust the questions on that document. So I ask that it be given a number and we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be marked for identification, MFI178.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And could I ask how long are you going to finish your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would Your Honour excuse me for one moment. I would think more than half an hour and less than an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Which means that we could not hear another witness for today, because, you know, if not, we have to send that witness back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that's -- that is what remains.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, definitely we'll finish this witness today?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I would think with some time to spare. Oh, except that - I forget - is Your Honour proposing to have a break?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Because we have to have a break at this time and we'll resume at 6.00, so we have an hour to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: For today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The break will have the effect of the questions going quicker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I hope so. Well, we will resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the legal discussions that took place, I was asking questions about the 9th of -- of September, and this is the -- after the first night that you say you spent in Jablanica. How did you get back to Grabovica the -- the morning of the 9th?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. A friend brought me there in his car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the friend?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some guys from Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us any names of those friends from Jablanica or not?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember now. It was 11, 12 years ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And -- but you're telling the truth, aren't you, that you really did get driven back by these men from Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And after the Karic meeting, as you've described it, you went back to Jablanica again for a second time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get there this time?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same way. I got a lift, hitch-hiked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... this time?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave you permission to go in to Jablanica and leave the place where you were billeted with your unit?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And -- well, Your Honour, could we please go into the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mehanovic, you've indicated that on the 9th after the Karic and -- the words that you ascribed to Vehbija Karic that you went back to Jablanica on that occasion hitch-hiking, did you see Ramiz Delalic in Jablanica that night?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Alispago?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you stay on that -- the night of the 9th?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, okay. And that's the same hotel you were referring to earlier; yes? The same hotel?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the only hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Were there any other members of the 9th Brigade with you on that second night?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Haris, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And what time did you go back the -- the following day, on the 10th, to the village of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. And prior to going back there, I take it you knew nothing about any killings in that village. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't get a translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, well, I'll put the question again. Prior to going back -- well, prior to arriving back in Grabovica on the 10th of September, you had no idea that anything terrible had happened in Grabovica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I heard about it when I got there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. And when you got back, the line-up which Ramiz Delalic had already conducted was well and truly finished; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't present during the line-up, but I heard from the soldiers that there was a line-up and that he had brought those children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And when you got back, did you see any signs of digging or covering up of bodies or massacres or murders of any sort?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I only saw that stain on the road. I don't know what that was. Something like blood or paint. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just going to put something to you from your evidence to the cantonal court on the 12th of January, 1999, a document I've already referred the witness to on a number of occasions, but this is on the third or fourth, the third page or fourth. Did you say this -- well, perhaps -- I'm going to read it to you and then I'll ask you some questions: "I cannot remember the date, but the day after the night when civilians in Grabovica were murdered Ramiz Delalic and Malco Rovcanin came and ordered us to line up. After we lined up, Delalic came up with two small children and asked them to recognise if some of us who were in the line murdered their parents. After they took a look at us, they said that none of us killed their parents. Later on Ramiz Delalic took them to Jablanica and I did not see them anymore. While I was there, apart from Ramiz Delalic lining us up, nobody else came to Grabovica to investigate the murder of the civilians." Now, is that true?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave that evidence, didn't you, to the cantonal court in 1999?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say it like that. I said what I said now, the same that I said in each statement, and that judge and the secretary who wrote that was practically illiterate. There are some things there -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to take you to another statement that you made that you already had read to you as well. This was a signed statement dated the 23rd of the 3rd, 1998. In that statement -- I just want to read a passage to you: "I spent that evening at home where I drank alcoholic drinks with my room-mates. When I woke up the next morning, I went for a breakfast. That is where we were informed that Ramiz Delalic, brigade deputy commander, ordered us to line up. After the whole assault company had lined up, Ramiz Delalic showed up bringing two children between eight and ten years of age with him. Ramiz told the children to pass by the ranks and see who had killed their parents. Only then did I realise that some ugly things had happened in Grabovica the night before. The two children walked by us, and after that they told Ramiz Delalic that none of the soldiers present had killed their father and mother. Except for the above stated, I am not familiar with any other details regarding the murder of the civilians in Grabovica." Now, Mr. Mehanovic, that's in the statement you signed. Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I am telling you again, I wasn't present when Ramiz Delalic brought those children. I was in Jablanica. Only after that did I come from Jablanica and I heard about these civilians being killed and how he had brought the children. I heard that from the soldiers. This was something that was talked about. This story spread.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I understand that you say that the judge at the cantonal court was illiterate, but you're not illiterate, are you? You can read and write; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're not someone who just signs whatever the police put in front of your nose, are you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never read those statements. Whichever one I signed, I never read it back, because I know what I said. Like I said, that statement by Nikolai, about 90 per cent of it are lies. There are words in it that I don't know how to say like that. It's just not written in my vocabulary, for sure. The way they wrote that and translated, it's one word and five people can say it in different ways. And if five different people say it, it would have a different meaning. I can only tell you what I know and what I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But I wasn't asking -- I wasn't asking about Nikolai, but anyway we'll move on from that at this stage, and I will now ask you about Nikolai. Did Nikolai -- that's Nikolai Mikhailov, the ICTY investigator, did he seem to you to be pushing your words in a particular direction?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he seem to you to be faithfully recording what you said or was he putting down what he wanted to hear, as far as you could see?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Germany, when they gave me that statement to look at, I saw that practically 90 per cent of things in there are untrue, for sure. I didn't even know that there was something like that written. I didn't read it back at the time when I signed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Mehanovic, on the night of the 10th, to the best of your memory, you left and went down to fight in Dreznica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think on the 10th, in the evening, at about 11.00. I'm not sure, but I think it was like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. And when you got down to Dreznica -- I just want to be clear about how things developed. Was there two -- two battles or two actions that you had to be involved in down there?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the first one an action concerned with Vrdi and the second one concerned with a mountain called Mount Medved?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And to the best of your recollection, did the first action, the one near to Vrdi, was it all finished in one day or did it take more than one day?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it went on the second day when we were on Mount Medved. There were some other people in the hills. The first day when it started, we were up in the hills. Then we returned, spent the night -- spent one night. And the next day we travelled for two days and two nights. We were walking, climbing on foot up the hill. And then when we got there, they were attacking Vrdi from below.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thanks. So it's really the timing as best you can remember now that I'm asking about, bearing in mind that it's quite a few years ago. You left on approximately the 10th, and would you say that you got into battle on a -- on around the 13th or 14th?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the first action was carried out around the 11th. We travelled all night, and the next day -- well, not the whole night. We travelled that night. When we reached Vrdi, in the morning then we started climbing. We were climbing during the day. And I think that during the day we attacked Vrdi. I think it was daytime when we were climbing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Look, I won't try to nail down precise dates and times at this length of time, but I just want to ask you about a couple of individuals down there. Did you meet with a couple of soldiers from Zuka's Unit who were good soldiers, actually, called Zuti and Popara?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not you encountered a journalist by the name of Sevko Hodzic during -- in fact, altogether, during your time in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I don't know that man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when you were fighting in these battles, do you recall whether or not those battles were featuring in the media back in Sarajevo? In other words, were you told that they were, or not?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. We weren't there. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I've just got a couple of structural questions about -- about certain units. There's been some reference here to a unit called the 2nd Independent Battalion commanded by Adnan Solakovic. Now, you're familiar with that -- that unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so that everyone is clear, that unit was not a 9th Brigade unit, was it?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a unit within the 9th Brigade called the 2nd Battalion, a different unit?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were four battalions, the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th -- or maybe even five. I am not sure, but it was most probably four rather than five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. But when we're talking about the battalion -- the 2nd Independent Battalion, which is the one that was down in -- in Grabovica, that unit was not connected to the 9th Brigade at all; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Adnan Solakovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was the commander of that unit.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks for that. And also, I have to ask you about an individual who was referred to in evidence I think by another witness, actually, called Juka Prazina. Do you remember the famous Juka Prazina?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We obviously don't have time to go into the whole history of Juka Prazina, but to your knowledge, he was not a member of the 9th Brigade, was he?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He had his own unit in 1992 in Sarajevo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for whatever reasons, they don't matter here, he ended up changing sides and fighting for the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He had nothing to do with your brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks. I've just got a couple of final questions now, and this is the last sequence of questions before I finish. There's been some allegations made that units in Sarajevo would sometimes take civilians to dig trenches. Now, I've got some questions about that. First of all, as far as you know, did all the brigades to a greater or lesser degree participate in that activity sometimes?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about all of them, but there were such stories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But as far as you know, the trenches simply had to be dug for military purposes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It depends. There was no trench-digging where we were. There was a tunnel that was dug underground, at Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But were you ever part of grabbing civilians and marching them off to dig trenches or tunnels, or not?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were not innocent civilians. These were smugglers in the market. As far as I know, we did not catch any civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were there any smugglers, to your -- to your direct knowledge, I mean - I don't mean speculation - but to your direct knowledge, were there any smugglers among the police -- the civilian police in the area where your unit, the 9th Brigade, was actually fighting against the enemy?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. Well, it's -- we've both had a long day, Mr. Mehanovic, but I'll try it again. During the time when you were fighting with the 9th Brigade in Sarajevo, did you know of any smugglers amongst the civilian police in your part of Stari Grad, the old town?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were such things. That -- the police officers had their people who sold things for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From time to time, was there a bit of irritation between the local civilian police, particularly the smuggling ones, and members of the 9th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether what happened?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. Did you notice any ill feeling between some of your soldiers in the 9th Brigade and some of the smuggling civilian police in your area?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't understand whether the witness said yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just excuse me one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thanks for your patience in answering the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we still have five minutes left. I don't think that we'll finish the redirect.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, since I might have a lengthy redirect, could we move on till tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Rather than break it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Well, witness, as I did before, I have to remind you once again you are still under the oath during your stay in The Hague, so do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I didn't even talk with anybody about the testimony. We were just talking about ordinary things. I am not -- I have nothing to discuss with anybody about the testimony. Why would I do that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm not blaming you. I just try to remind you of this fact, as I did to any other witnesses before this Court. Yes. Having said that, I think the hearing is adjourned. We will resume tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
